featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a wonderful lunch at Rasoi and everything was simply delightful!
• Firdausi Aloo – Perfectly spiced, rich and flavourful with a royal touch.
• Karari Rumali Roti – Crisp, light and beautifully done with the right crunch.
• Corn & Water Chestnut Starters – Fresh, crunchy and a great balance of sweetness and spice.
• Aromatic Green Thai Curry – Fragrant, creamy and packed with authentic flavours.
• Zafrani Rasmalai – Soft, melt-in-the-mouth and infused with delicate saffron notes.
• Anar Ka Pyaar (Mocktail) – Refreshing, fruity and perfectly balanced.
• Thanda Teekha (Mocktail) – A fun blend of sweet and spicy that really stood out.
The service was quick and seamless, and the staff was extremely knowledgeable about the menu, offering great recommendations. Since we visited on Holi, they surprised us with complimentary Jalebi Rabdi and Thandai, which made the celebration even more special.
A truly memorable dining experience — highly recommended! 🌸✨

featured_reviews.name: Akshaya Vishwakarma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this place, and the experience was absolutely wonderful. The ambience is cozy, aesthetically pleasing, and perfect for a relaxed meal.

For drinks, I tried the Virgin Mojito and Oreo Milkshake, and both were refreshing and delicious. As starters, we ordered the Rasoi Paneer Tikka and Bhatti Da Murg, which were flavorful, perfectly cooked, and truly satisfying.

For the main course, we had Paneer Nimbu Da Pyaaza with Rumali Roti and Schezwan Fried Rice. Both dishes were excellent, packed with flavor, and complemented each other really well.

To finish the meal, we indulged in their Rasmalai, which was the perfect ending—soft, rich, and absolutely delightful.

Overall, everything from the food to the ambience exceeded expectations. A highly recommended place for anyone looking to enjoy great food and a pleasant dining experience!

featured_reviews.name: Mansee Nisar
featured_reviews.review_text:

annar ka pyaar, cranberry delight.

featured_reviews.name: Foodie Crown
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Rasoi near Dadar Station and had a wonderful dining experience. The restaurant offers a great mix of North Indian, Malwani, and Chinese cuisine, making it a good option for groups with different food preferences.

We started with the Chicken Sheekh Kebab and Chicken Tikka, both of which were flavorful, juicy, and perfectly cooked. For the main course, we tried the Thai Curry, which was rich, creamy, and packed with authentic flavors.

To accompany our meal, we ordered a Fruit Punch mocktail that was refreshing and well-balanced. We ended the meal with their Sizzling Brownie, which was served hot and was the perfect sweet treat to finish on.

The food quality, taste, and portion sizes were impressive. The service was prompt, and the location near Dadar Station makes it a convenient spot for a satisfying meal. Definitely worth a visit if you're in the area and looking for delicious food across multiple cuisines.

featured_reviews.name: Shraddha Viswakarma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Rasoi recently and honestly, it’s one of those places that just gets everything right. The ambience and decor are super aesthetic yet warm, making it perfect for literally anyone—families, couples or even chill friend scenes.

The place was quite packed when we went, but the crowd added to the vibe instead of feeling chaotic. Service was genuinely top-notch—staff was quick, polite and very attentive.

We tried the Watermelon & Basil Martini and Anar Ka Pyaar—both refreshing and beautifully presented. Starters like Balinese BBQ Chicken and Sigri Murgh were full of flavour and perfectly cooked. For mains, the Nawabi Murgh with Butter Garlic Naan was rich and comforting, and the Chicken Dum Biryani was aromatic and satisfying.

They also had a live singer which elevated the whole experience. Ending it with Mango Kulfi Falooda (seasonal aamras specials!) was just perfect. Great food, great vibe, and totally worth it.

featured_reviews.name: Aafreen Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a wonderful experience at Dadar Rasoi! It’s a perfect place to visit with family and loved ones. The ambience is warm and welcoming, making it a great spot to celebrate birthdays, anniversaries, and special occasions.
The live music adds a lovely vibe to the dining experience, and the service was excellent throughout our visit. The staff was polite, attentive, and made us feel comfortable.
The food was absolutely delicious — everything was well-cooked, flavorful, and served fresh. Every dish tasted amazing and was prepared with great quality.
Highly recommended for anyone looking for good food, good music, and a memorable time with family or friends. Must visit this place!

featured_reviews.name: Pranali Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Rasoi is an amazing place for authentic North Indian comfort food. The food tastes just like simple, fresh, and full of flavour.

We tried their North Indian dishes and everything was perfectly cooked. and the food was not oily or heavy.

Great hygiene, good portions, quick service, and affordable prices.
Perfect spot 😍😍
Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: tanishka_on_the_go
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited Rasoi in Dadar East and had a wonderful experience. The ambience is very pleasant and comfortable, perfect for a relaxed meal. The staff is extremely polite, attentive, and makes you feel welcome. We tried the Tamarind Ginger Sour and Fruit Sangria, both were refreshing and well balanced. The Sigri Murgh was smoky and full of flavour, cooked perfectly. Chicken Patiala Seekhan and Nukkad Wali Biryani were absolutely delicious and rich in taste. Kombdi Wade was authentic and comforting. We ended the meal with in-house Kulfi Falooda which was amazing. Overall, Rasoi has great food, great service, and a lovely vibe. Highly recommended 👍

featured_reviews.name: J G Irani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Food and friends make the best memories. So true! These are created at Dadar Darbar.
Dadar Darbar the most happening food and beverage restaurant set in a train dining car right outside Dadar East Station is a must visit for Mumbaikars and people travelling to Mumbai. Dadar Darbar is an affordable value for money, no frills, full on service, conveniently located restaurant. Dadar Darbar serves you North Indian menu with a twist. They create and cook up a fusion of indian, regional and international tastes for different palates.
For starters we had kheema paav, chicken lollypop, surmai fry, chicken spring roll. Whereas Hyderabadi chicken biryani was fulfilling as the main dish. For deserts we had Afghani dryfruits ice cream, Caramel custard and the Arabic pudding.
At Dadar Darbar, good food creates good mood!

featured_reviews.name: viraj s wadkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Darbar is a lifesaver for late-night travelers! The best part is that it’s open the whole night, so if you miss your last local train, this place feels like a cozy train compartment just a few steps from the station – literally next door!

The restaurant maintains good hygiene, which is a big plus, and the staff is polite. Service can be a little slow when it’s crowded, but that’s understandable. The food taste really surprised me – much better than expected!

If you’ve had a long train journey and need good food without traveling any further, this is the perfect spot. Convenient, clean, and satisfying late-night cravings right near the station!

featured_reviews.name: Huzefa Rangwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s a nice theme to have a restaurant in an old train compartment. Gives a different feel. Apart from the looks the food is actually good. It really tastes good. It’s not a fine dine restaurant so don’t expect amazing service but it was a good experience.
Since it is just outside the station, it is convenient if you have just arrived and are hungry. It’s affordable too, not too expensive.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Gaikwad.
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dadar Darbar in Dadar East has become one of our go to places, and for good reason. We’ve visited many times, and the experience has consistently been wonderful. The food is genuinely delicious, rich in flavor, well prepared, and always satisfying. Whether it’s a quick meal or a relaxed outing, the quality never disappoints. What truly makes the place stand out is the service. The staff is polite, attentive, and always ready to help with a smile. A special mention goes to Mr. Irshad, who has attended our table on multiple occasions. His service is exceptional courteous, prompt, and very thoughtful. He makes sure everything is just right, which adds a personal touch to the entire dining experience.
The ambiance is comfortable and welcoming, making it a great spot for family visits as well as casual dining. Overall, Dadar Darbar offers a perfect combination of tasty food, great service, and a friendly atmosphere. We always look forward to coming back and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a satisfying meal in Dadar East.

featured_reviews.name: Roshani Batra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Primarily, a delivery outlet Charcoal eats serve awesome quick bites to munch on as late as 3 am during weekends and till 11 pm during weekdays. The place has seating arrangements too which I assume that hardly anybody show up for dine in whereas like most of us opt for delivery service from the outlet. It offers amazing biryanis and quick bites as the brand says it all - 'bite that good' and yes we do bite it good from Charcoal Eats. The delivery is outstanding with organised colourful packaging. I happened to go on for trying out their famous biryani and some quick bites right at their outlet in Dadar east. I found the interiors very attractive and cosy. Since the place has famed itself more into delivery but otheriwse I think it is also a chill place to dine in with family and friends.
Talking about my yummilicious orders, I had-
1) Peach Ice Tea - They serve beautiful glass bottles of 'Brewhouse' Peach Ice Tea. Its cute as well as amazing drink to opt for with the meal aside.
2) Barbeque Loaded Fries- Crispy potato fried topped with bbq sauce and some spicy masala were tasting too good when eaten hot.
3) Chicken Mughlai Paratha- Chicken chunks and onion mixture loaded inside fried parathas tasted just like the rolls.
4) Chicken Tikka Biryani- Reasonable price for the awesome biryani. Small chicken chunks beneath the fine layered biryani can be good to go to try this one.
5) Salted Caramel Mousse- The salty and sweet taste of this chocolate mousse is divine. Although not their in house production, but still this one would be loved be loved by all the sweet lovers just like me.
I totally loved this vibrant place. And it serves awesome quick bites and biryanis and moreover at decent price that could be the relevant reason for quick hogging to opt for from the same.

featured_reviews.review_text: I placed an order for Burger and drink (non alcoholic strawberry bear). The Biryani's too good. So I tried something different this time. The burgers were nice. Fresh quality buns and good stuffing. 3.5/5

featured_reviews.name: Heena Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Charcoal eats is my go to place for Biryani now, especially after trying other places! This time I ordered vegetarian and vegan dishes like Dum Baked Jackfruit Biryani, Afghani Makhmali Vegetarian Biryani, Dum Baked Aloo and Corn Biyani, Smoked Paneer Makhani Rice bowl and Kathal Haleem. As always they are of high quality, right quantity and worth the price. It comes in sustainable packaging making it a guilt free takeout choice.
I have noticed that usually when I takeout from anywhere, Non vegetarian food tastes way better and I always take advantage of choosing it as I live in a vegetarian house. While the Non vegetarian menu is fantastic, the vegetarian and vegan dishes are equally good! Thats why for the first time ever, I was thrilled to just order the vegetarian and vegan variants and I had no FOMO!
Charcoal eats definitely proves ‘Veg biryani is not biryani’ wrong! The Kathal Haleem is so creamy and imagine getting it all year round :O
Thank you for making such good Biryani and other dishes!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Heena,

We're delighted that you loved our food and service.
We hope to keep serving you like this and assure you of our best, always!
Please do keep giving your feedback.
Stay connected for latest updates on Facebook & Instagram @charcoaleats

Cheers,
Team Charcoal Eats

featured_reviews.name: RCD thefoodie
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nobody would deny to the fact that "Charcoal eats" serves some of the best variations of biryani in town.
I absolutely love their food and being weekend we wanted to relish in some of their new flavours that we haven't tried  so we ordered some & needless to say right from packaging to taste to quality everything was amazing.
This is what we all ordered
*Ustaadi hyderabadi mutton biryani - If you like spicy chatpata biryani then do try this, mutton pieces were very soft & tender.
*Makhmali afgani chicken tikka  biryani - Absolutely loved this, mild flavoured creamy biryani with juicy pieces of grilled chicken.
*Chicken baida mughlai paratha - paratha was stuffed generously with mince chicken and was done perfectly.
*Lucknowi seekh kebab - Ahh truly delicious! Melt in mouth and that mint curd chatni was perfect accompliment.
*Oh and also do not miss ordering the best danedaar and creamy phirni, one of the best.
*Vilayati chocolate mousse - Velvety texture with perfect balance of sweetness & that after taste of dark chocolate is fab.
Washed of everything with cranberry flavoured fruit beer.
Finally how can i forget the complementary junior chocolate pan😍
Our weekend was perfectly sorted with the scrumptious food by charcoal eats.

featured_reviews.name: Anas Sk
featured_reviews.review_text:
So we visited this outlet in Dadar(East). The outlet was surrounded with a number of gardens.

Beginning with the food we tried the barbecue loaded fries here, believe me when I say they're excellent, these are the best ones I've had till date. The precise amount of sauces in it was just so perfect.
The next thing we tried was peach ice tea with chicken mughlai paratha they were so crisp and fresh, but I felt like there were a little dry, the flavor was wonderful but left my throat parched, anyway the iced tea worked wonders there it was a relief to have them. However iced tea had a bit of excess flavoring still it was pretty good and brewed very well.

Lastly I had the classic chicken Biryani and salted Caramel mousse, the Biryani was so delicious also decorated wonderfully also the grains were pretty separated even after cooling down, mousse was lovely. I am so in love with it now!

I really love it so much.

Coming to the ambience the lighting was nice and cosy type and the ambience was decorated in light shades, making it perfect for pictures.

Servicing was polite and quick.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Anas,
Thank you very much. Glad you liked our food. We look forward to serve you again.
Regards,
Team Charcoal Eats

featured_reviews.name: Team The Food Guruji
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a very small outlet situated in a very peaceful surrounding of Five Gardens area. Just a 10-15 mins walk from either wadala stations or Dadar station.

So started with some shakes and juices.

I ordered for Watermelon Juice and i must say this was one of the freshest ..i dont know wheather this was a proper word.. but yes this was so fresh . I just loved it. Totally Recommended .Even the grape juice i tried was great.

Then came in the fries. I loved that we ourselves need to add the masala to the fries and make it for ourselves. I love that process. 3 fries which i tried. Garlic Cheese , Mexican and Tandoori. All 3 were great but the garlic cheese is a must try fries when you visit here.

Pizzas were the next in line up. I loved the new pizza bas which they use that is the puff . It tastes like the khari which we have with tea . This is something different and was nice. 4 Cheese with the puff base was great.

Finally the biryanis arrived . I tried 4 biryanis.

Classic Lamb

Classic Chicken

Butter Chicken

Afghani Chicken

Basically these biryanis are not the authentic biryanis but who care... ITS BIRYANI...

I loved the Classic Chicken and Classic Lamb . They are the must try over here.

Also One thing which i loved was the packing of these biryani boxes. High quality of packing and very well arranged in the boxes. You get the cutlary and raita within the box with a special raita masala which was SUPERRR SE UPARR...

In the end it was time for some desserts.

Main attraction over here is the Strawberry Souffle . Its the best . Dont forget to try that one.

Chocolate mousse and caramel mousse were okayish i can say.

Overall its a pocket friendly on a higher side type of food joint. Its a must visit place. The manager whose name i have forgotten but wont forget him is a very nice host i must say. Having a smiling face throughout .

Do visit this place.

My rating would be a 4/5
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello,
Thank you very much. Glad you liked our food. We look forward to serve you again.
Regards,
Team Charcoal Eats

featured_reviews.name: Karl Kolah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Have ordered from Charcoal eats after a while and the taste remains the same, which is absolutely yum.

An important thing while delivering is the packaging and the restaurant did a very good job, no spills, perfect containers and the starters come in a box which had the chutney and cut onion in the side making it very easy to order and eat.

In the starters the Afghani Malai Chicken Tikka are a must have. In main their mutton biryani was delectable, soft meat perfect flavours and lovely rice. These two would be my absolute favourites in the order. The Smoked butter Chicken Biryani is a good option if you are a fan of butter Chicken and Koyla Chicken Tikka tastes good with a charcoal flavour.

Overall a great and satisfying meal. Looking to order soon.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Jondhale
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Malhar recently for lunch and ordered a variety of dishes, including Crab Lollipop, Prawns Koliwada, White Rice, Rava Bombil, and Agri-style Chicken Curry. We had also planned to try Amboli and Bhakri, but unfortunately, both were out of stock.

The Crab Lollipop and Prawns Koliwada were flavorful and well-prepared. However, the Agri-style Chicken Curry did not meet expectations. The use of garam masala was overpowering, and the excessive black pepper (kalimiri) affected the overall taste, though the dish was still edible.

The ambience of the restaurant was very beautiful, but I noticed some issues with cleanliness. For example, one of the glasses provided still had food particles stuck on the edge where a person drinks. I requested the steward to replace the glass; he took the dirty one but forgot to bring a new glass altogether, leaving me to drink directly from the bottle.

While the food was average overall, I was particularly disappointed with the service. Both the steward and the captain seemed uninterested and inattentive. Despite repeated requests, it took them over 15 minutes to bring tissues, even when asked clearly and politely.

Additionally, the Prawns Koliwada was served nearly 40 minutes later, after we had almost finished our main course. At that time, only 3–4 tables were occupied in the restaurant, so such a delay was unjustified. When I raised this issue with the captain, his casual response was, "Humare yaha thoda late hi hota hai." This type of attitude is not expected from a reputed establishment like Malhar.

In summary, although the ambience was nice and some dishes were good, the poor service, lack of attention to cleanliness, and indifferent staff attitude significantly impacted our overall dining experience.

The place has a simple yet comforting vibe, and the aroma itself sets the mood as soon as you walk in. The food is absolutely top-notch—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. From crispy dosas to soft idlis and rich sambhar, everything tasted authentic and satisfying.

The service was quick and efficient, and the staff was polite and attentive throughout. It’s one of those places where you go for the food and end up loving the whole experience.

If you’re in Dadar and craving real South Indian flavors, this spot is definitely worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text: Café Muthuswami in Dadar is a cozy spot that brings authentic South Indian flavors to life. Known for its crispy dosas, soft idlis, and rich, aromatic filter coffee, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The ambiance is simple yet inviting, perfect for casual catch-ups or a relaxed solo meal. Service is quick, and the food quality is consistently impressive. Whether you’re craving a hearty breakfast or a light evening snack, this café delivers on both taste and experience. A must-visit for anyone who loves traditional South Indian food in Mumbai with a homely touch and great value.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Fulsundar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami Cafe is located just outside Dadar East railway station, so it’s very easy to find and perfect for a quick stop after travel. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, which is nice if you want to sit comfortably or just grab something quickly.
We tried the strawberry milkshake & mango milkshake both were thick, chilled, and refreshing. The paper masala dosa was big, crispy, and came with good chutney and sambar. Kanchipuram idli was soft and flavourful, a little different from regular idli and worth trying.
Cheese tava rice was spicy, cheesy, and filling good if you’re very hungry. We ended with pineapple sheera, which was warm, slightly sweet, and had a nice fruity taste.
Overall, it’s a good place for South Indian food and quick snacks near the station.

featured_reviews.name: VISHAL UPADHYAY
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered cheese pav bhaji, and masala dosa and both were extremely delicious. We loved both the items. Cost wise it appeared a little costly given the ambience, and quality of service. It was situated near Dadar railway station and is fine for some snacking.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re in Dadar and craving authentic South Indian flavors any time of the day, Muttuswami Cafe is the place to be!
This is the only café in the area open 24/7, making it a perfect spot for early breakfasts, late-night cravings, or casual meetups at any hour.
The food quality is outstanding, with every dish served fresh, flavorful, and satisfying:
Cheese Pav Bhaji – perfectly buttery with a generous layer of melted cheese that elevates the classic taste.
Podi Idli – soft, bite-sized idlis coated beautifully in spicy podi masala and ghee.
Muttuswami Special Benne Dosa – rich, crispy, and soaked in butter with a delicious traditional touch.
Spring Dosa – a unique fusion twist, crispy outside with a flavorful stuffed filling inside.
Fruit Custard Dessert – creamy, refreshing, and loaded with fresh fruits for the perfect sweet ending.
Their fresh juices are equally impressive — especially the pomegranate juice and the orange-mosambi mix, both refreshing and naturally sweet.
What truly makes the experience special is the warm and polite staff. The service is quick, attentive, and always delivered with a smile. The beautiful interiors create a clean, cozy, and welcoming atmosphere, making you want to sit back and enjoy your meal.

featured_reviews.name: imran khan
featured_reviews.review_text:

Food was amazing tasty. A little higher price.. people may feel for this .. however if you compare to food outlets in the mall .. it's the same. Combos one can have .. quantity fulfills  the hunger for one person. Overall nice experience. Recommended if around Dadar railway station.

featured_reviews.name: Taran Arora
featured_reviews.review_text: If you enjoy South Indian food and want a cleaner, more café-style experience in Dadar, Mutuswami is worth trying. Best dishes to order are Benne dosa, thatte idli, rasam rice , filter coffee and pineapple sheera.  Staff is very courteous and welcoming.

featured_reviews.name: Mithil Thakker
featured_reviews.review_text:

They have indoor and outdoor seating. Post 8 pm it's a busy schedule for the restaurant so go a bit early to get the best available table of the house.

Our food recommendations.

Podi Idli:
You have to visit this place to experience this extraordinary delicacy of the house .

Benne Masala Dosa:
This one won't disappoint you if you are fond of benne then definitely give this a try.

Pav Bhaji:
Again a house supremacy. Spicy and Tangy burst of flavours with every bite .

The Mango Milkshake was rich and thick  . Even their cold coffee has a supreme vibe.

Pineapple Sheera .
When at a South Indian cuisine specialist restaurant then you can't miss this legendary dish . Indeed a heavenly experience.

Overall a delightful experience as always.

Happy and Safe Fooding Until Next Time.

featured_reviews.name: Rutuja Gaikwad
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pritam Da Dhaba is one of those places that truly lives up to its reputation. Yes, it is quite expensive compared to regular dhabas, but once you taste the food, you understand why people keep coming back.
The ambience has a classic dhaba vibe with a comfortable and well-maintained setup, making it perfect for family dinners as well as outings with friends. The service is quick, polite, and well managed, even during rush hours, which adds a lot to the overall experience.
Coming to the food — this is where Pritam Da Dhaba really shines. The Punjabi flavours are rich, authentic, and full of taste. The gravies are perfectly spiced, buttery, and cooked to perfection. Every dish feels fresh and well prepared, and the quality of ingredients is clearly noticeable. Portion sizes are decent, and the presentation is neat.
Although the pricing is on the higher side, the taste, consistency, and overall dining experience make it worth the money. It’s not an everyday spot, but definitely a place you visit when you want to treat yourself to good Punjabi food.
Overall, Pritam Da Dhaba is expensive but absolutely worth it for the taste, quality, and experience. Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys authentic Punjabi cuisine and doesn’t mind paying a little extra for it. 🌟🍽️

Reaching on time is of utmost importance as they serve limited periods over lunch and dinner. Here is my honest opinion:

1. Hygiene - Fresh, neat and clean as expected from an ex hotelier

2. Value for money - Yes. A wholesome serving of half plate chicken biryani would be at INR 80 while a full plate serving of the same is at INR 150 with a tiny portion of raita which is negligible

3. Flavor - Nothing exceptional but true to basic Biryani options you would find around the city but prepared by Mr. Parkar and his parents diligently

4. Overall - A one time visit is ideal if you are in Dadar but travelling especially for this is not recommended

I think this one has caught the online hype Machine bug really well.

We started of with the corn and cheese dumplings and tge sauce they served had the most authentic flavour, next we tried the chilli paneer where each paneer cube was soft and melted in the mouth. To end the evening on a sweet note i ordered my ever favourite sizzling brownie with vanilla ice cream in top it had the perfect taste and shahi tukda was amazing too. What I loved about this restaurant is the cosy interiors and paintings on the wall this added to the charm of our city mumbai!

We started off with Paneer Pahadi Kabab and Chicken Laasooni Kabab – both were packed with flavors and perfectly cooked. For the main course, we tried Smokey Butter Chicken and Mushroom Masala paired with chapati and steamed rice. The butter chicken especially stood out – rich, creamy, and truly a treat.

To end the meal on a sweet note, we had Shahi Tukda and Sizzling Brownie with Vanilla Ice Cream. The sizzling brownie was the ultimate showstopper – warm, gooey, and indulgent.

Overall, great food + good vibes = highly recommended! Definitely a must-visit spot in Dadar, especially since it’s right next to the famous Dadar Flower Market

featured_reviews.name: Tanishka Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Dadar Retreat recently and had such a wonderful experience. It’s a cozy dining spot that starts serving snacks from 8 AM and goes on till late drinks at 1 AM, which makes it perfect for any time of the day. The place is divided into two sections, making it ideal for families, couples, or even large groups.

The menu is quite versatile, but their Chinese and South Indian dishes really stand out. I tried the LIIT and Piña Colada, both refreshing and well-balanced. For starters, the Prawns Koliwada and Chicken Sholay Kebab were full of flavor and cooked perfectly.

In mains, the Chicken Bhuna with Tandoor Roti was a comforting combination and absolutely delicious. Ended the meal with a Caramel Pudding, which was the perfect sweet note to finish on.

Overall, the food, service, and ambiance all come together beautifully at Dadar Retreat. Definitely a must-visit spot if you’re in the area!

During our conversation, I shared that I am from Delhi and thoroughly enjoyed experiencing these authentic Irani dishes in Mumbai. Her hospitality, combined with the food, made the outing truly memorable.

Overall, Café Colony is not just about food—it’s about warmth, tradition, and conversations. A must-visit gem in Dadar.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

This place truly gave me a heartwarming experience and the kind of food that reminds you what real, honest cooking tastes like. It’s amazing to know that this restaurant has been around for over 102 years, carrying forward a legacy of authentic flavors and consistent quality. You can really feel that heritage in every dish they serve.

The food was absolutely delicious and clearly made with care and good-quality ingredients. I loved how every bite had that traditional touch — nothing fancy, just pure, flavorful food made right. My personal favorites were the Mutton Sanju Baba and the Haleem. The mutton was soft, juicy, and full of flavor, while the haleem was rich, creamy, and perfectly spiced — the kind that instantly makes you smile after the first spoonful.

The ambiance adds to the experience — simple, calm, and full of character. It feels like a place where stories have been shared for generations. The staff was really friendly and attentive, making sure we were comfortable and enjoying our food.

Overall, I’d say this isn’t just a restaurant it’s a part of culinary history. If you love traditional, soulful food that warms both your heart and your stomach, this place is a must-visit.

The highlight, of course, is their legendary chicken dishes—especially the Chicken Sanju Baba, which is packed with bold spices and has a rich, indulgent taste. The food overall is delicious, with generous portions and that proper old-school Mumbai Mughlai flavor.

The ambience is simple and no-frills, but that’s part of its charm. It’s more about the food than the setting. The place is usually quite crowded, and you might have to wait a bit for a table, especially during peak hours.

Service is quick considering the rush, though it can feel a bit hectic at times. Hygiene and seating are decent but not luxurious, so it’s best to go in with the right expectations.

Overall, Noor Mohammadi is a must-visit if you’re looking to enjoy authentic, hearty Mughlai cuisine in Mumbai. It’s not about fine dining, but about great taste and a truly local food experience.

featured_reviews.name: Ansari Anas
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a very disappointing experience today at this restaurant.

Right from the beginning, the service was poor. The staff member who took our order was unclear and seemed to lack proper knowledge of the menu. Then, the order itself was completely messed up the first starter was incorrect, and another starter that was supposed to be half was served as full.

We also ordered an Arabic juice in a small size, but instead, a large size was served without informing us, leading to unnecessary extra charges.

The service overall was extremely poor. Items that we never ordered were added to our bill. On top of that, soup was brought to our table without us even ordering it — if we had consumed it by mistake, we would have been charged for that as well.

Lastly, the staff’s behavior was unprofessional, and the person taking the order lacked basic courtesy and communication skills.

This entire experience was unacceptable, and I would strongly advise the management to improve both service quality and staff training.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Karaday
featured_reviews.review_text:
Great Taste, but Minor Hygiene Concern

I recently visited Arabian Darbar Restaurant in Mazgaon, and I must say, the food was incredibly tasty! The rich flavors and authentic touch to each dish made the dining experience truly enjoyable.

However, I did encounter a small issue as I found a strand of hair in one of the dishes. While this was a bit disappointing, the overall quality of the food and the restaurant's ambiance almost made up for it. I hope the management can pay extra attention to hygiene to ensure a consistently positive dining experience.

Despite this hiccup, I would recommend the restaurant for its delicious offerings and hope they address the minor hygiene concern for future patrons.
